description: Over a ten-year window 39% of Nigerian refugee claimants were approved against an overall acceptance rate of 58%. CBC's analysis put Nigerian acceptance at 46% between 2018 and September 2024, against an overall recognition rate that rose to 82% in the first nine months of 2024.
energy_note: Half the odds of the average claimant, on the same evidence standard.

description: Between 2013 and 2024 Canada's Refugee Protection Division denied 13,171 Nigerian applications and accepted 10,580, putting Nigeria consistently among the top five countries for asylum denials, peaking at 3,951 refusals in 2019.
energy_note: Thirteen thousand refusals from one country.

description: An immigration lawyer describes cases from countries with historically lower acceptance rates, like Nigeria, as always sent to hearings - where the claimant must prove the police cannot protect her and that she could not be safe anywhere else in the country.
energy_note: No paper decision. Always the room, always the cross-examination.

aspect: EXAMPLE - 'she could have moved to a large city'
description: The Canadian Association of Refugee Lawyers challenged the IRB's decision to set as a legal precedent its denial of a Nigerian woman's claim based on female genital mutilation, where it was found she could have relocated to one of Nigeria's large cities. Internal flight alternative is the mechanism by which a real danger becomes a survivable one on paper.
energy_note: The cutting was real. The finding was that she should have moved.

aspect: The UK route narrows at the certification stage
description: The UK initial grant rate across all nationalities fell from a record 76% in 2022 to 47% by 2024 and 39% currently. Claims certified as clearly unfounded under section 94 carry no in-country appeal, and since 28 June 2022 section 94(3A) means a certified claim carries no appeal at all.
energy_note: Refused, certified, and no appeal exists.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the returns agreement, by the numbers
description: A UK-Nigeria returns agreement targeted 961 Nigerian asylum seekers with no appeal rights remaining and 1,110 foreign national offenders in prisons. In the year ending September 2025 Nigerians ranked among the top five nationalities claiming asylum after entering the UK on a valid visa, and the Home Office said this led it to tighten visa and asylum grants to Nigerians.
energy_note: A quota with a nationality on it.

description: She cannot name the date her uncle came to the house, because she was fourteen and there was no calendar on the wall. The determination notes the inconsistency between her screening interview and her substantive interview and finds her account not credible. Everything she said was true.
energy_note: Disbelieved over a date she was never told.

aspect: The waiting is the punishment even when you win
description: Years without the right to work, on subsistence support, in accommodation chosen for you, with the case reopening at intervals. A grant at the end does not return the years.
energy_note: Four years of not being allowed to work.
